Ashby Mill Lofts | Partl Evaluation of Significance Page 1 of 6

Description of physical appearance

i. The building is a five-story brick textile mill with a heavy-timber interior frame,
segmental-arched window openings and a stepped parapet along Bridge Street.

2. The ground floor retains its original loading doors on the river elevation. Upper
floors are open loft spaces divided by rows of timber columns at regular bays.

3. A stair tower and a later boiler house stand at the east end. The boiler house is
a non-contributing addition and is excluded from this evaluation.

4. Date of construction: the mill was constructed in 1912 for the Ashby Cotton
Manufacturing Company and operated as a spinning mill until 1958.

+ Alterations: several ground-floor openings were infilled in the 1960s. Roofing
and most mechanical systems have been replaced over time.

Ashby Mill Lofts | Partl Evaluation of Significance Page 2 of 6

Statement of significance

6. The mill is significant under Criterion A for its association with the textile
industry that shaped the economy of Danville in the early twentieth century.

Vs It is also significant under Criterion C as an intact example of slow-burn mill
construction, with heavy timber framing, brick bearing walls and large daylight
windows.

8. The building contributes to the district through its scale, materials and its
relationship to the river and the adjacent warehouse blocks.

Ashby Mill Lofts | Partl Evaluation of Significance Page 3 of 6

Integrity
9. The building retains integrity of location, setting, design, materials,
workmanship, feeling and association. Infilled openings are reversible.
10. The historic window openings remain legible on all elevations, although a large
share of the original sash has deteriorated.
11. Interior timber columns, beams and maple flooring survive on most floors.

Project summary

1. Proposed use: residential rental with ground-floor commercial space. The
completed project will contain apartments on floors 1 to 5 and two commercial
suites on the ground floor.

2. Estimated rehabilitation start: October 2023. Estimated completion: mid-2025.

FS The rehabilitation will be carried out as a single project, with the upper floors
completed in sequence.

4. Architect: Hollins and Reade Architects, Richmond, Virginia.

Ashby Mill Lofts | Part2 Description of Rehabilitation Page 2 of 24

Conditions of approval

Condition 1 The historic east stair shall be retained in place. Any new railings shall
be simple in design and attached so that they can be removed later
without damage.

Condition 2 Replacement windows must replicate the original wood profiles in
material, dimensions and muntin pattern. Shop drawings for
replacement windows must be submitted to and approved by NPS
before installation.

Condition 3 Exposed timber columns and beams shall not be sandblasted or covered
with new finishes.

Please send the information required by Condition 2 to the State Historic Preservation

Office, which will forward it to the National Park Service.

Item 1 - Site work
Existing feature and condition: Regrade the area along the river elevation to drain
away from the foundation. Existing granite curbing will be retained and reset.
Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and .
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.
Item 2 - Masonry
Existing feature and condition: Repoint deteriorated mortar joints with a lime-based
mortar matched to the original in color, texture and strength. Replace spalled brick
only where necessary, with brick matched in size and color.
Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Ashby Mill Lofts | Part2 Description of Rehabilitation Page 4 of 24

Item 3 - Roof
Existing feature and condition: Replace the existing built-up roof with a new
membrane roof. The stepped parapet will be repaired and capped. No rooftop
additions will be visible from Bridge Street.
Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.
Item 4 - Windows
Existing feature and condition: The building has 412 historic window openings. Sash
that can be repaired will be repaired. Sash too deteriorated to repair will be replaced
with wood units replicating original profiles, as set out in the window survey.
Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Ashby Mill Lofts | Part2 Description of Rehabilitation Page 5 of 24

Item 5 - Doors
Existing feature and condition: Original loading doors on the river elevation will be
repaired and fixed in place, with new glazed doors set behind them.
Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.
Item 6 - Interior layout
Existing feature and condition: Upper floors will be divided into apartments. Corridors
will follow the line of the central column bays so that the timber columns remain
exposed.
Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Ashby Mill Lofts | Part2 Description of Rehabilitation Page 6 of 24

Item 7 - Structure

Existing feature and condition: Timber columns and beams will be retained and
cleaned with low-pressure methods. Damaged members will be sistered rather than
removed.

Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Item 8 - Floors

Existing feature and condition: Maple flooring will be retained and refinished where it
survives. New flooring in wet areas will be laid over the existing boards.

Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Ashby Mill Lofts | Part2 Description of Rehabilitation Page 7 of 24

Item 9 - Stair tower

Existing feature and condition: The historic east stair will be retained in place as an
exit stair, with code-required handrails added.

Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Item 10 - Mechanical systems

Existing feature and condition: New heating and cooling equipment will be placed on
the roof behind the parapet and within apartment closets. Ductwork will run in
corridors, not across exposed beams.

Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Existing feature and condition: New wiring will be concealed in partition walls. Light

Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Existing feature and condition: A new sprinkler system will be installed with exposed

Proposed work and impact: the work will be carried out to the Standards and
documented in the attached photographs and drawing sheets.

Market and Feasibility Study
           Ashby Mill Lofts, Danville, Virginia | Prepared by Piedmont Realty Advisors | May 10, 2023

Executive summary
1.       This study evaluates market demand for the conversion of the Ashby Mill into rental apartments with
         ground-floor commercial space.
2.       The subject will contain 84 apartments and 2 commercial suites. The study concludes that the market
         can support the project at the proposed rents.
3.       The analysis relies on a field survey completed in April 2023, public demographic data and interviews
         with local property managers.




Ashby Mill Lofts | Market and Feasibility Study                                                     Page 1 of 32

Market area
4.       The primary market area covers the City of Danville and the adjacent portions of Pittsylvania County
         within a fifteen-minute drive of the River District.
5.       Employment in the market area is concentrated in healthcare, advanced manufacturing, logistics and
         public administration.

Demographics
6.       Household growth in the market area has been modest but steady, with the strongest gains among
         renter households aged 25 to 44.
7.       Median household income in the River District has risen faster than the city average since 2019, driven
         by new employers near the riverfront.




Ashby Mill Lofts | Market and Feasibility Study                                                      Page 2 of 32

Rental supply
8.       The surveyed market-rate rental properties report stable occupancy and limited new supply in the
         downtown area.
9.       Most competitive properties were built between 1985 and 2005 and offer fewer amenities than the
         proposed project.

Comparable properties
10.      Three converted warehouse and mill properties in the region were surveyed. All report waiting lists for
         loft-style units.
11.      Rents at comparable properties have increased between three and five percent a year over the last three
         years.




Ashby Mill Lofts | Market and Feasibility Study                                                      Page 3 of 32

Proposed rents
12.      Proposed rents for the subject are positioned slightly above the newer garden-style properties,
         reflecting the historic character and downtown location.
13.      The unit mix is weighted toward one-bedroom units, which matches the profile of renter households in
         the market area.

14.      Demand from new renter households, turnover in the existing stock and in-migration supports the
         proposed number of units.
15.      The capture rate required for the subject is within the range considered achievable for a project of this
         type.
